### Reference: runtime internals

#### `permissionArgs`

function · `import { permissionArgs } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The Node flags that run a child under the permission model (stable in Node 22.13+): `--permission`, one
`--allow-fs-read` / `--allow-fs-write` per absolute path, and `--allow-child-process` / `--allow-worker` only when
declared.

```ts
function permissionArgs(grants: ProcessGrants): string[];
```

#### `ProcessGrants`

interface · `import { ProcessGrants } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What a child may touch under Node's permission model.

```ts
interface ProcessGrants {
  /** Folders and files it may read (its bundle, its folders, the loader it runs under). */
  readonly read: readonly string[];
  /** Folders it may write (its state, data and cache). Writable folders are readable too. */
  readonly write: readonly string[];
  /** What `system.json`'s `permissions` declares; both default to no. */
  readonly permissions?: SystemPackageManifest['permissions'];
}
```

Refers to: [`SystemPackageManifest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.package-ts#core-systempackagemanifest).

#### `CrashPolicy`

class · `import { CrashPolicy } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The restart rule for supervised processes, one per supervisor, keyed by instance: an asked-for stop or a clean exit
(for `on-failure`) stops; the restart code restarts at once; a crash restarts after `backoff`, doubling with each
crash in the last hour, and more than `maxPerHour` crashes in an hour gives up (the caller may roll back).

```ts
class CrashPolicy {
  constructor(options: CrashPolicyOptions);
  /** Decide what follows `exit` of the instance `key`, run under `policy`; `stopping` when the stop was asked for. */
  decide(key: string, policy: RestartPolicy, exit: Pick<ProcessExit, "code">, stopping: boolean): ExitDecision;
  /** Forget an instance's crashes (after a rollback, a new version or an uninstall). */
  forget(key: string): void;
}
```

#### `CrashPolicyOptions`

interface · `import { CrashPolicyOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

How `CrashPolicy` decides.

```ts
interface CrashPolicyOptions {
  /** The longest wait between restarts (`HARNESS_SUPERVISE_BACKOFF_MAX`). */
  readonly maxWait: number;
  /** The exit code that asks for an immediate restart (`RESTART_CODE` unless the supervisor sets another). */
  readonly restartCode: number;
  readonly clock?: (() => number) | undefined;
}
```

#### `ExitDecision`

type · `import { ExitDecision } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What to do after a process exits.

```ts
type ExitDecision =
| { readonly action: 'stopped' }
| { readonly action: 'restart-now' }
| { readonly action: 'restart'; readonly wait: number; readonly crashes: number }
| { readonly action: 'give-up'; readonly crashes: number };
```

#### `AllowlistProxy`

class · `import { AllowlistProxy } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

An HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1 that lets through only allowed hosts: `CONNECT` tunnels for https, forwarding for http.

```ts
class AllowlistProxy implements NetworkGate {
  constructor(options: AllowlistProxyOptions);
  /** Listen on a free port of 127.0.0.1; resolves to the proxy's URL. */
  start(): Promise<string>;
  setAllowed(allow: readonly string[]): void;
  /** Stop listening and cut every open tunnel. */
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

#### `AllowlistProxyOptions`

interface · `import { AllowlistProxyOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

What an allowlist proxy lets through, and who hears of what it refuses.

```ts
interface AllowlistProxyOptions {
  /** The hosts let through at first (`grants.network`, plus the hub's own); `setAllowed` changes them. */
  readonly allow: readonly string[];
  readonly onRefused: (refusal: ProxyRefusal) => void;
  /**
   * Where an allowed target is connected to: the address it was checked at (resolved once, so a name that resolves
   * elsewhere a moment later can't move the connection), or `undefined` to refuse it. Absent, the host as named.
   */
  readonly route?: (target: ProxyRefusal) => Promise<string | undefined>;
}
```

#### `NetworkGate`

interface · `import { NetworkGate } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

#### `McpFace`

class · `import { McpFace } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The system's native fns as MCP tools, with its resources and commands beside them, and the server and transport that offer them.

```ts
class McpFace implements McpToolSource {
  /** `contexts` fills the system's commands as prompts (the system runtime). */
  constructor(table: SystemTable, env: RunEnvironment, version: string, limits: McpLimits, contexts: ContextTexts);
  /** The MCP server (JSON-RPC: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/*`, and `resources/*` and `prompts/*` when the system has them). */
  get server(): McpServer;
  /** The tools offered now. */
  tools(): McpTool[];
  /** Run the fn behind a tool; `undefined` when there is no such tool. */
  call(name: string, args: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<McpToolResult | undefined>;
  /** Fns added or removed at runtime change the tool list. */
  onChange(listener: () => void): () => void;
  /** Serve over stdin/stdout or Streamable HTTP. Resolves once listening (stdio serves until stdin ends). */
  serve(how: McpServe): Promise<void>;
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
```

#### `LlmWire`

class · `import { LlmWire } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

aeye → wire for the parts where callers differ in what the wire can't carry.

```ts
class LlmWire {
  constructor(options: LlmWireOptions);
  /** An aeye message as it crosses the wire or is saved. Provider caches and reasoning details stay behind. */
  message(message: Message): LlmMessage;
  /**
  * An aeye request as JSON: each schema as its lenient JSON schema (or as sent, `schemas: 'sent'`); an empty tool
  * list is left out.
  */
  request(given: Request): LlmRequest;
}
```

Refers to: [`LlmRequest`](context:fs/authoring.core-types.llm-ts#core-llmrequest).

#### `LlmWireOptions`

interface · `import { LlmWireOptions } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

How `LlmWire` treats what the wire can't carry.

```ts
interface LlmWireOptions {
  /**
   * `refuse` throws a `LinkGap`, for requests that will be sent on (a lossy request would reach the model changed).
   * `placeholder` keeps going, for records: an unsendable part's content becomes `[binary content]`.
   */
  readonly unrepresentable: 'refuse' | 'placeholder';
  /**
   * `lenient` (default) writes each schema as its lenient JSON schema, the code shape: what a forwarded request carries.
   * `sent`, for records: a request a provider planned is written as the model was sent it (its tools in the model's
   * dialect, the dispatcher in place of the tools behind it, the output as rendered for it); one not planned, lenient.
   */
  readonly schemas?: 'lenient' | 'sent';
}
```

#### `deferredProblems`

function · `import { deferredProblems } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

The deferred values of a forwarded request that don't read back through the schema they were written for, once

tool and what was wrong. Values with no tool (written as they are) aren't checked.


#### `AnswerDecoder`

class · `import { AnswerDecoder } from '@harness/sdk/server'`

Decodes what a model wrote through the plan its request was sent with (the one the provider pinned, else a lenient
one) as the stream passes, so a system reads every answer in the code shape and decodes it with its own schemas:

- a finished tool call (`toolCall`) is decoded (`plan.decodeCall`: strict `null`s back to absent, pairs back to
  records, JSON text parsed): its arguments become the decoded value's JSON, under the tool's own name. One that
  doesn't fit keeps the model's arguments and says why in `invalid`, the message the model is told; arguments that
  aren't JSON at all go as they are (the system's prompt reports them). A call that already has `invalid` (decoded
  by a provider further along) goes as it is.
- a call to the dispatcher (more tools than the provider takes) names its tool only in its arguments, so it is held
  back until it's complete and goes as one chunk, named and finished, under the tool it reached.
- a structured answer's text is held until the answer ends (its `finishReason`, or the stream's end) and goes as one
  chunk of its decoded value's JSON, or as the model wrote it when it doesn't decode.

Partial arguments (`toolCallArguments`) of other calls stream as they come, in the model's shape. One decoder per
stream; its first chunk is read after the provider planned the request.

```ts
class AnswerDecoder {
  constructor(request: Request);
  /** What to send for one chunk the model streamed: nothing, the chunk (decoded), or at the answer's end the answer first. */
  chunk(chunk: Chunk): Chunk[];
  /** What is still held when the stream ends: the structured answer, decoded. */
  end(): Chunk[];
  /** A finished tool call, decoded (see the class). */
  call(call: ToolCall): ToolCall;
  /** A structured answer's text, decoded: its value's JSON, or the text as it is when it doesn't decode. */
  answer(text: string): string;
}
```
